earnings_release.text: EX-99.1 2 ex991_earningsreleasex3q26.htm EARNINGS RELEASE Document 3Q26 FINANCIALRESULTS BNY Reports Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Per Common Share of $2.34 NEW YORK, October 15, 2026 – The Bank of New York Mellon Corporation (“BNY”) (NYSE: BNY) today has reported financial results for the third quarter of 2026. CEO COMMENTARY BNY delivered strong results in the third quarter. With broad-based growth across our platforms, we increased revenue by 12% year-over-year, delivering significant operating leverage and earnings per share growth of 24%. For the quarter, we generated a very solid pre-tax margin of 39% and a strong ROTCE of 29%. Our performance in the quarter once again highlights the resilience and durability of our business model against the backdrop of an overall constructive but uneven operating environment. Client demand continued to grow, underpinned by our ongoing work to unlock the value inherent in the combination of BNY’s businesses enabled by our platform operating and commercial models. Sales and pipelines remained very healthy across products, client segments and regions and we launched several solutions during the quarter that are meeting emerging needs in the market. Looking ahead, our teams around the world are energized by BNY’s momentum and excited about the opportunities in front of us to create value for our clients and shareholders. – Robin Vince , Chief Executive Officer EPS Pre-tax margin ROE ROTCE $2.34 39% 16% 29% (a) KEY FINANCIAL INFORMATION (dollars in millions, except per share amounts and unless otherwise noted) 3Q26 vs. 3Q26 2Q26 3Q25 Selected income statement data: Total fee revenue $ 4,078 1 % 12 % Investment and other revenue 175 N/M N/M Net interest income 1,423 (2) % 15 % Total revenue $ 5,676 — % 12 % Provision for credit losses 1 N/M N/M Noninterest expense $ 3,489 1 % 8 % Net income applicable to common shareholders $ 1,608 (5) % 20 % Diluted EPS $ 2.34 (4) % 24 % Selected metrics: AUC/A (in trillions) $ 63.4 1 % 10 % AUM (in trillions) $ 2.2 (2) % 2 % Financial ratios: 3Q26 2Q26 3Q25 Pre-tax operating margin 38.5 % 39.8 % 36.4 % ROE 16.0 % 17.2 % 13.7 % ROTCE (a) 29.0 % 31.3 % 25.6 % Capital ratios: Tier 1 leverage ratio 5.7 % 5.9 % 6.1 % CET1 ratio 10.9 % 11.0 % 11.7 % HIGHLIGHTS Results • Total revenue of $5.7 billion, increased 12% • Noninterest expense of $3.5 billion, increased 8% • Diluted EPS of $2.34, increased 24% Profitability • Pre-tax operating margin of 38.5% • ROTCE of 29.0% (a) Balance sheet • Average deposits of $311 billion, increased 4% year-over-year and decreased 1% sequentially • Tier 1 leverage ratio of 5.7%, decreased 42 bps year-over-year and 24 bps sequentially Capital distribution • Returned $1.4 billion of capital to common shareholders • $436 million of dividends • $937 million of share repurchases • Total payout ratio of 86% year-to-date (a) For information on the Non-GAAP measures, see “Explanation of GAAP and Non-GAAP financial measures” beginning on page 9 . KEY DRIVERS (comparisons are 3Q26 vs. 3Q25, unless otherwise noted) • Total revenue increased 12%, primarily reflecting: • Fee revenue increased 12%, primarily reflecting net new business, higher client activity and higher market values, partially offset by the mix of AUM flows. • Investment and other revenue decreased primarily reflecting the impact of fixed income and equity trading activity, seed capital results and the absence of a 3Q25 disposal gain, partially offset by other investment gains. • Net interest income increased 15%, primarily reflecting the reinvestment of investment securities at higher yields and balance sheet growth, partially offset by deposit margin compression. • Provision for credit losses was $1 million. • Noninterest expense increased 8%, primarily reflecting higher revenue-related expenses and investments, partially offset by efficiency savings. • Effective tax rate of 22.8%. Assets under custody and/or administration (“AUC/A”) and Assets under management (“AUM”) • AUC/A increased 10%, primarily reflecting higher market values, net client inflows and net new business, partially offset by the unfavorable impact of a stronger U.S. dollar. • AUM increased 2%, primarily reflecting higher market values, partially offset by cumulative net outflows and the unfavorable impact of the stronger U.S. dollar. reference.summary: The Bank of New York Mellon Corporation provides a range of financial products and services in the United States and internationally. It operates through Securities Services, Market and Wealth Services, Investment and Wealth Management, and Other segments. The Securities Services segment offers custody, trust and depositary, accounting, exchange-traded funds, middle-office solutions, transfer agency, services for private equity and real estate funds, foreign exchange, securities lending, liquidity/lending services, and data analytics. This segment also provides trustee, paying agency, fiduciary, escrow and other financial, issuer, and support services for brokers and investors. The Market and Wealth Services segment offers clearing and custody, investment, wealth and retirement solutions, technology and enterprise data management, trading, and prime brokerage services.
